newsitem.title: UK: London freight - Atlantic quiet, Pacific firm.
newsitem.headline: London freight - Atlantic quiet, Pacific firm.

text.p: Prompt positions remained difficult for capers and panamaxes in the Atlantic in relatively quiet conditions but the Pacific was firm for these sizes in virtually all dates and positions, brokers said.
With April Atlantic fixtures showing a premium over March, together with the situation in the Pacific, the Baltic Freight Index (BFI) rose nine points to 1,490.
Geared tonnage was little changed and the Baltic Handy Index gained just 3 points to 1,103.
GRAIN - Halla covered a spot U.S. Gulf/Japan stem of 52,000 heavy grain with CSK Fortune at $24.50 no combo.
Last reported in this trade was Boesen's fixture of Andre tonnage at $25.50 no combo, but that was for loading second half April.
Vessels were booked for grain business from Argentina and Brazil, although not all fixtures were fully reported.

Finagrain for example, was understood to have taken a prompt panamax on timecharter to load 25,000 tonnes from Plate and Necochea to the east Mediterranean, and Worthington was linked with the Cabral-relet Paulette 50,597 dwt delivery spot Paranagua for a trip to the Continent, both on private terms.

Transcatalana was reported to have covered 50/52,000 tonnes soyabean meal 54' plus 3,000/4,000 tonnes heavy grain from Paranagua to Spanish Mediterranean for end March/early April at a firmer $17.00 basis 15 days.

The 1972-built Pioneer-relet Magnum 68,326 dwt was reported by some to have been nominated for Pioneer's own business, but others said the vessel may have gone to Grain-Coop Paranagua/Lisbon-Hamburg range at $16.50 basis 13 days.
Simeon CH 61,700 dwt was booked by Casinomar delivery retroactive sailing Hamburg March 10 trip via E.C South America redelivery Far East at $12,000 daily but failed on subjects.
In the Far East, the Halla-relet Win Trader 73,000 dwt which had agreed $13,000 daily delivery Tokyo Bay end March trip via Australia to Mideast Gulf with E.A.S.T. also failed on subjects.

Fresh orders included Continental for a panamax delivery Vitoria March 20/30 for two laden legs redelivery Skaw-Cape Passero, and Toepfer 25,000 tonnes heavy grain up river Plate/Taiwan for March 28/April 5.
MINERALS - Early capers were struggling in the Atlantic. Vakis T 130,000 dwt, fixed by Deiulemar delivery prompt ex drydock Lisbon for a U.S. Gulf coal round trip at $9,500 daily, failed on subjects.
This followed the similar failure of Tigris 123,000 with Pan Ocean dwt delivery Rotterdam early April for four months redelivery Skaw-Cape Passero at $8,100 daily.
Sesagoa fixed Princess Clipper for 110,000 iron ore Goa/Ijmuiden for April/May loading on private terms.
Some newbuilding caper period fixtures were concluded with Far East delivery but it was not always possible to pinpoint the rates.
Bocimar took Aqua Faith 166,000 dwt delivery ex-yard South Korea April 15/30 for five to seven months in the low $16,000 daily. Some brokers said the rate was $16,750.
Shinwa was reported to have fixed Tien Yang Hai 169,000 delivery ex-yard China end April for seven to nine months at either $17,500 or $17,900 daily.
Panamaxes were also covered for period trade in the East.

Transfield was linked with Mass Wits 69,355 dwt delivery south China April for 12 months at an undisclosed rate, and Safmarine took Artemis 68,000 dwt delivery prompt south China for a trip via Bunbury to Richards Bay at close to $12,000 daily, with the option of five to seven months timecharter at $11,500 daily.
At 1545 GMT the BIFFEX futures stood five to 29 points weaker. Most Active April traded last at 1,612 and sold 34 lots. Total volume was 97 lots.
